note: Tests that fail on the Linux runner for reasons that do not exist on this Mac. The Mac allowlist (unit-known-red.json) does NOT transfer: it names this machine's environment, and the nightly runs ubuntu-24.04-arm. An entry here is a claim with evidence, not a mute button — check it with `node local/check-nightly-linux-parity.mjs --failures <downloaded-artifacts>`, which fails on any red that is not listed and reports a listed test that passed as prunable. An entry stores Vitest's full name, describe chain included, and pins the cause with `match`; a bare title no longer absorbs anything, and an entry with no `match` that is not `flaky: true` is a problem. The 2026-11-05 upstream move of this file (2f217b4d0dd) left its entry naming a path no report contains, so the red it exists to absorb was not being absorbed at all until #317 corrected the path, the name and the cause together. 2026-11-24: pruned 5 entries, which empties `entries`, because upstream #46786 (2cffdeda72c) deleted all four spec files they named — the daemon history-recovery, headless offscreen browser, queued-stop row and updater prerelease-feed suites. Three were upstream environment reds. The two updater cases were the fork's own REST-list-first delay cases: `local/sync/upstream-deleted-fork-tests-baseline.json` accepts the file's retirement; ten of its cases are re-homed in `src/main/updater/releases/updater-fork-feed.test.ts`, but the whole REST-list-first delay describe block is absent there — the two titles listed above and the newest-past-the-delay and no-feed-timestamp cases with them — so the fork's delay coverage is gone rather than re-homed. Nothing is left to absorb, so an empty `entries` is the fail-closed state rather than a widening: with nothing listed, every Linux shard red fails its job until a red is classified with evidence. Each pruned entry keeps the `match` and `flaky` it was recorded with, so a re-add does not have to re-derive the cause, and an entry naming a file this tree no longer has is exactly what `tests/tools/unit-gate.test.mjs` fails on — which is why the five are recorded here rather than still listed.

unhandledErrors.evidence: monaco-editor's own CancellationError raised when the editor is disposed; the stack names no repository file and no test. Observed on both machines, in runs whose only named failures were already triaged.

LOCAL-PATCHES.md records a node-runtime worker dying mid-run on this pool; it names no test, and the run it came from had every named failure already triaged. The Mac manifest carries the same headline, but only this entry sets `explainsFailure: false`: the shard verdict judges a Linux shard against its assignment, and a worker that died can lose tests inside a file the report still lists, so a crash cannot be the only explanation for a failed shard — it is tolerable only beside a known red that already explains the exit. `local/gate-unit.mjs` does not read the field.

The browser-mode dev server cannot serve Monaco's TypeScript worker from the dependency store — the URL embeds the store path, which differs per machine and per runner. No repository file appears in it and no test asserts on it.
